## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The production change to an exact `"REPORT v1"` match is correct, and `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` covers it. `test_rejects_legacy_header` does not test what it claims to test and should be fixed or removed. The policy manifest lists no policy files.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:11 — tests — `"v0".join(fixture.rsplit("v1", 1))` replaces only the last `v1`. That `v1` is in the body line `version=v1`, so the test parses `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`. This input keeps the supported `REPORT v1` header and has no `END` line. `parse_report` returns `None` at `app/report.py:3` because `END` is missing, so the version check at `app/report.py:5` never runs. The comment at line 9 ("changing the fixture's version to v0") describes a header change that never happens. Could you use a literal complete report with a legacy header, such as `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`, or drop this test because line 15 already covers that case? — The test cannot fail if the version check is removed or reverted to `startswith("REPORT ")`, so it gives false confidence that it guards the new check.

## Strengths
- `tests/test_report.py:15-17` sends a report with a valid `END` line and a `REPORT v0` header. Only the new check at `app/report.py:5` rejects that input, so the test would fail if the check regressed.
